title: Nobody wanted to fund this AI video startup. Now it's worth $4 billion

scenes.label: DEAL ROOM
scenes.narration: January 2026. Investors put two hundred million dollars into a London AI startup and value it at four billion dollars. But for years, almost nobody believed in it.

title: THE STARTUP THAT
MADE VIDEOS TALK
scenes.subtitle: THE SYNTHESIA STORY
scenes.narration: This is the story of Synthesia, the company that turns typed text into videos with AI presenters.

scenes.label: RESEARCH LAB
scenes.narration: It starts with a research paper. Victor Riparbelli, who had worked in Danish startups, reads work by researcher Matthias Niessner and sees a business inside it.

scenes.label: LONDON
scenes.narration: In 2017 they start Synthesia in London, with Steffen Tjerrild and UCL professor Lourdes Agapito. Four co-founders, years before anyone talked about generative AI.

scenes.label: PRODUCT 1.0
scenes.narration: Their first product is an AI dubbing tool. It changes a speaker's mouth movements, so a video can match a new language.

scenes.label: INVESTOR PITCH
scenes.narration: Raising money is hard. Victor later said their first rounds were sold on a story that just did not resonate much with investors.
A tiny team, a strange idea, and a technology that many people find a little scary. For a while, the future is not clear at all.

scenes.label: FIRST BELIEVER
scenes.narration: One early believer is the American investor Mark Cuban. Victor has said Cuban was their very first investor.

scenes.label: THE BIG MOMENT
scenes.narration: Then, April 2019. A malaria charity film shows David Beckham speaking nine languages, made with Synthesia's technology. Suddenly, the world notices.

scenes.label: HIRING
scenes.narration: The same month, Synthesia announces a three point one million dollar seed round. Now they can hire.

scenes.label: THE NEW IDEA
scenes.narration: The product grows from dubbing into something bigger: type a script, and get a video with a digital presenter. No camera, no studio.
By December 2021, the company is valued at three hundred million dollars. Companies use it to make training videos fast.

scenes.label: DEAL ROOM
scenes.narration: June 2023. A ninety million dollar round led by Accel, with Nvidia joining, makes Synthesia a unicorn, worth one billion dollars.
January 2025. Another one hundred eighty million dollars, led by NEA, at a two point one billion dollar valuation.

scenes.label: REPORTEDLY
scenes.narration: In 2025, Adobe reportedly held talks to buy Synthesia for about three billion dollars. According to press reports, no deal was made.

scenes.label: SERIES E
scenes.narration: Instead, in January 2026, GV, the venture arm of Google's parent Alphabet, leads a two hundred million dollar round at four billion dollars.
Reports say its yearly recurring revenue has passed one hundred million dollars. Next, Synthesia wants AI agents that talk with employees and help them learn.

scenes.label: YOUR DESK
scenes.caption: TRY IT FREE
scenes.narration: So how can you use it? Synthesia has a free plan. Type a script, pick a stock AI avatar and a language, and get a short video with a watermark.

scenes.caption: LINK IN DESCRIPTION
